name: Power and Cooling
blurb: Grid connection, generation, and thermal management.

items.name: Datacenter electricity demand
items.note: DOE's 2024 LBNL report: datacenters consumed about 4.4% of US electricity in 2023, projected to reach 6.7 to 12% by 2028 - AI is the driver

items.name: The liquid-cooling transition
items.note: Blackwell rack systems are liquid-cooled by design; 120kW-class racks ended air cooling's run at the AI high end

items.name: PUE and efficiency reporting
items.note: Google publishes fleet-wide power usage effectiveness (trailing twelve-month ~1.1) as the reference efficiency disclosure

reading.body:
Datacenter electricity demand is rising from 4.4% of US consumption in 2023 to a projected 6.7 to 12% by 2028, driven primarily by AI workloads, according to the Department of Energy's 2024 analysis.

This trajectory reflects a hard constraint on AI scaling. The grid cannot expand as fast as compute demand grows. Even modest adoption of AI training and inference at scale will require either new generation capacity, storage, or load shifting, none of which are built yet. The range of the projection (6.7 to 12%) signals uncertainty about how fast AI deployment actually happens, which depends on factors the electricity numbers alone cannot capture.

Thermal management has become the technical gate. Blackwell-class systems require liquid cooling by design, ending the era of air-cooled racks at the frontier. This shift is not optional efficiency gain; it is necessary for density and power delivery. A datacenter built to air-cool 50kW racks cannot absorb 120kW liquid-cooled ones without full infrastructure redesign.

Google's power usage effectiveness metric (approximately 1.1 on a trailing twelve-month basis) is the operational standard for disclosure and comparison. This measures overhead: how much total energy the facility consumes per unit of compute delivered. The metric is useful for tracking how much building and cooling losses matter relative to the chips themselves. It does not measure aggregate consumption, only efficiency, and does not account for embodied emissions or regional grid carbon intensity.
